questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.explanation: Binary search repeatedly divides the search interval in half, resulting in logarithmic time complexity O(log n).

questions.question: Which data structure follows the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle?
questions.explanation: A Queue processes elements in the order they arrive — First In, First Out (FIFO).

questions.question: What does DNS stand for and what is its primary function?
options: Domain Name System — translates domain names to IP addresses
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) acts as the internet's phonebook, converting human-readable domain names into machine-readable IP addresses.

questions.question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
options: Processes are lightweight, threads are heavy
Threads share the same memory space within a process
questions.explanation: Threads within the same process share memory and resources, making them lighter than processes which have isolated memory spaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a lossless compression algorithm?
questions.explanation: PNG uses lossless compression, preserving all original data. JPEG and MP3 are lossy formats.

questions.question: What is Big O notation primarily used for?
options: Describing the worst-case asymptotic upper bound of an algorithm
questions.explanation: Big O notation describes how the runtime or space requirements grow relative to input size, focusing on scalability.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a mutex in concurrent programming?
options: To provide mutual exclusion and prevent race conditions
questions.explanation: A mutex (mutual exclusion) ensures that only one thread can access a critical section of code at a time, preventing data corruption.

questions.question: Which paradigm does SQL belong to?
questions.explanation: SQL is a declarative language — you specify what you want, and the database engine determines how to retrieve it.
